hook.belief: Every cryptocurrency runs on a blockchain.
hook.gap: If OneCoin had no blockchain, what were people really paying for?

scenes.narration: Prosecutors say OneCoin never had a real blockchain. It still raised four billion dollars.
scenes.visual_intent: A chain of linked blocks snaps apart within two seconds while a counter rolls to four billion.

facts.claim: Prosecutors say OneCoin had no true, verifiable blockchain.
OneCoin took in more than $4 billion from victims worldwide between 2014 and 2016.

scenes.narration: So its bosses handed out coins that existed nowhere, not even on their own ledger.
scenes.visual_intent: A private table where a caret types balances into rows that no chain records.

facts.claim: By about March 2015 Greenwood and Ignatova were allocating to members OneCoins that did not exist even in OneCoin's purported private blockchain.

scenes.narration: Yet people believed. Dr Ruja Ignatova sold it at Wembley Arena as the bitcoin killer.
scenes.visual_intent: An arena from the back rows: spotlights find an empty mic and the crowd lights up wave by wave.

facts.claim: In the summer of 2016 Ruja Ignatova took the stage at Wembley Arena and promoted OneCoin as the bitcoin killer.

scenes.narration: Instead, buyers paid for coin packages, sold member to member.
scenes.visual_intent: Package cards of growing size fill with coin glyphs while a dotted line climbs past them (illustrative sizes).

facts.claim: Members bought OneCoin packages through its multi-level marketing network.

scenes.narration: But recruiting paid commissions, so the real product was the next recruit.
scenes.visual_intent: A recruitment tree grows with money climbing every edge, then each coin badge is crossed out and stamped with a barcode.

facts.claim: OneCoin paid members commissions for recruiting others to buy OneCoin packages, a pyramid scheme.

scenes.narration: Until October 2017, when the woman at the top flew to Athens and vanished.
scenes.visual_intent: A flight path draws from Sofia toward Athens and the radar ping fades out before landing.

facts.claim: On 25 October 2017 Ruja Ignatova boarded a flight from Sofia to Athens and has not been seen since.

scenes.narration: In 2022 the FBI added her to its Ten Most Wanted list. Like the blockchain, she was never found.
scenes.visual_intent: A case file is stamped, then the broken chain from the first shot returns as wreckage.

facts.claim: In 2022 the FBI added Ruja Ignatova to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list.
Ignatova has not been found since boarding the October 2017 flight (as of the January 2023 report).
